review_notes: I read the whole file, lines 1–348. It declares no @[simp] lemmas and no simp-set definitions, so the simp interface here is only what the file uses from other libraries. The local declarations are `linearIndependent_pow_of_transcendental`, `exists_mul_aeval_eq`, `finrank_le_finrank`, `natCard_places_le`, `finiteDimensional_adjoin_of_coe_eq`, `adjoin_adjoin_subset`, `adjoin_range_eq_top` and `solution`. They are statements for explicit use, not rewrite rules. The only local rfl-style identity is `he` inside `finiteDimensional_adjoin_of_coe_eq`. It is a private proof-local fact, and marking it simp would not be justified. The proofs use simp mostly as `simpa`, `simp only` with explicit lemma lists, or `by simp` for small side goals, so no unwanted expansion shows up in the text. The long `attribute [-simp]` and `[-instance]` lines at the top look like generated environment boilerplate that removes simp lemmas from other files. They are not a defect in this file's own interface. I saw no competing rules and no credible rewrite cycle. I did not open the imported theorem files to check how their simp lemmas interact with this file's `simpa` calls. I also could not check by running Lean whether any of those calls is fragile.
